tests.narrative: The original forgetting curve fits S2 with D=0.153 — far below the extraction threshold, confirming memory decay as a natural retention process.

tests.narrative: A 130-year replication of Ebbinghaus. S2 wins on AIC versus the power law (ΔAIC≈−28; AIC 17 vs 45). D=0.219 — the retention law is reproducible.

tests.name: Gloria Mark attention (2004–12)
tests.narrative: Attention-span decline across 2004–2012 crosses the D=1 threshold (D=1.232), indicating algorithmic extraction rather than natural decay.

tests.name: Gloria Mark attention (2012–22)
tests.narrative: From the NPA manifesto: attention collapse accelerates after 2012 (D≈4.28) — a deep-extraction regime as short-form feeds dominate.

tests.name: ETH hourly (crypto HFT)

tests.name: SPY daily (equity index)
tests.narrative: Broad equity index shows D=0.711 — natural retention. The market aggregates enough actors to stay below the extraction cliff.

tests.narrative: Tech-heavy ETF sits exactly at the threshold (D=1.016). Consistent with the concentration of algorithmic flow in tech names.

tests.name: Stock holding period (1940–80)
tests.narrative: Pre-digital holding-period decay already shows D>1 (1.559) — extraction is not purely an HFT phenomenon; it predates electronic trading.

tests.name: Stock holding period (1980–2023)
tests.narrative: Modern era sits on the threshold (D=1.005) with a near-perfect fit (R²=0.999). The entire post-1980 regime is at the extraction boundary.

tests.name: Trade duration (1980–2000)
tests.narrative: Trade-duration retention decays with D=1.781 — extraction. The perfect fit (R²=1.000) reflects the regularising effect of electronic matching.

tests.name: Trade duration (2000–2023)
tests.narrative: HFT era: D=2.454 — deep extraction. The doubling of D versus the prior era quantifies the acceleration of fictitious-capital turnover.

tests.name: SFR density decline (z=2→0)
tests.narrative: Star-formation-rate density declines with D=3.458 — the cosmos is in an extraction regime as dark energy suppresses structure formation.

tests.name: Bound structure growth decline (z=1.5→0)
tests.narrative: Bound-structure growth decays with D=2.571 — extraction. Hierarchical clustering is being starved by accelerated expansion.

tests.name: Cluster growth decline (z=1→0)
tests.narrative: Cluster-growth retention: D=2.608, R²=0.999. Same family as SFR — the universe is losing its capacity to build bound objects.

tests.name: NV nanodiamond 40nm, room temp

tests.name: NV nanodiamond 3μm, room temp

tests.name: NV nanodiamond 40nm, ~6K

tests.name: NV ensemble, 100ppm N impurity
tests.narrative: Dense 100ppm ensemble: D=0.527. Higher impurity does not induce extraction — the retention law governs T₂ echo decay uniformly.

tests.name: Ising spatial T=1.5

tests.name: Ising crossover T=2.269 (critical)
tests.narrative: At the critical temperature Tc≈2.269, simple exponential wins on AIC; S2 sits exactly on the D=1 cliff (D=1.088). A falsification boundary for the law.

tests.name: Quantum magic accumulation (random circuits)

tests.name: Magic filament ridges (random circuits)

tests.name: D_eff scales with qubit count

tests.name: Transpilation preserves S2

tests.name: Sweden FTT (1984–91)
